exposure: ABO blood group incompatibility (newborns with A/B blood groups born to O-positive mothers)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 1455 healthy term and near-term newborns (males 50.8%, females 49.2%) born to O-positive mothers.
finding: ABO incompatibility (newborns with A/B blood groups born to O-positive mothers) was associated with an increased incidence of hyperbilirubinemia (29.4% and 35.8% respectively), and transcutaneous bilirubin measurement in the early days of life can be used as a screening tool for critical hyperbilirubinemia in this group.
